svg.title: Proof. The first statement interchanges a finite sum with an absolutely convergent series. For the converse consider the moment vectors m(t) = ((t/p)n)n ∈l∞. The hypothesis says that P j cjm(tj) 7→P j cjf(tj) is a well-defined linear map of norm at most C on their span, hence on its closure. The coordinate vectors lie in that closure: subtract the already recovered lower coordinates from m(t) at small t ̸= 0, divide by (t/p)n and let t →0. Their images are the coefficients an, and m(t) = P n(t/p)nen converges in norm after restriction to radius p′ < p by the geometric majorant.
